paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Chanina and Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi. Coming from the south, he brought a teaching, Sukkah 54a; Sotah 24b. In Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name: “The southern elders said,” Berakhot 18b; Chullin 132b. Also in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name, Berakhot 8, end of b. Rav Huna’s student. In Rabbi Abbahu’s name in Rabbi Assi’s name, Yevamot 65b; Rabbi Ammi’s name, Rabbi Assi’s name, Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Sanhedrin 41b; Rabbi Assi’s name, Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Menachot 103a, Sanhedrin 41b—several things. “Abaye said” (I think Rabbi Ammi should be read) “in Rabbi Assi’s name,” Yevamot 101a. In Rabbi Assi’s name in Resh Lakish’s name, Shabbat 45b; see Tosafot. He went out in patched shoes in the market, Shabbat 114a. Menachot 32, beginning of b: if he altered either, invalid; Rabbi Acha permits. In Rabbi Achai bar Chanina’s name—R.Sh.K.’s reading. Shabbat 79b: Rav Acha son of Rabbi Chanina; some say in Rabbi Yaakov bar Chanina’s name. Nedarim, chapter 3, 22b: Rav Adda son of Rabbi Chanina—perhaps an error. Rav Nachman in his name, Chullin 132b. Yuchasin’s “Rav Tavla in his name” is false. Rabbi Levi in his name, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 2, mishnah 4, on “One who reads backward has not fulfilled.” Shmuel bar Nachum was his mother’s brother or his mother’s father.
